title: Has someone seen a complete list of RPG Maker plugins?

posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body:
Back in 2018, I had found a website that had a great list of RPG Maker plugins mostly for RPG Maker VX Ace. I have moved onto other versions, but I lost the link to the website. It was back during one of the competitions and I had stumbled upon Galv's scripts and I was trying to make an 2.5D isometric on MV. The website had a grey theme. It had toggles on the left side for which version of RPG Maker. I believe the search bar was a bit above it. Has anyone ever heard or seen something like it?
If there is no complete list, would someone official be interested in starting one? If not, maybe I could throw something on here or Wikipedia. It would be really great if there was a built-in repository inside RPG Maker. Or I might be able to add my own tools like from this
post
.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Just as a quick bit of terminology - RPG Makers XP through VX Ace used scripts. RPG Makers MV and MZ use plugins.
And no, I've never heard of any complete list of plugins (or scripts). I don't know if it's even remotely plausible with all of the different sites and forums for different countries and languages with people dropping bits of code in there.
SigmaSuccour had a Google Sheet that he used to accumulate plugins, but I have no idea if he still updates it, if it covers non-English stuff, or even where (if) he's still active.

posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body:
Maliki79 said:
Nope.  I have them all on pastebin.
If there's a good reason, I'll be happy to move em.
Click to expand...
Sort of, the reasons I thought about it was for backups, documentation, or version control. I thought it might be easier for you in the long run. I enjoy GitHub desktop for most projects, but it allows for straight Git when I need CI/CD.
I am going to start making a tool so users can download scripts directly to their RPG Maker folder. There is a small difference between hosting on GitHub and Pastebin, but most users will notice nothing. The tool should allow users to easily download plugins without scouring the internet for hours for an 3D, action, or isometric plugin. I like SigmaSuccour's list and as a community, everyone can help improve it a bit.
Even after I have the tool up and running, I can see there are configuration issues. Some people will need tutorials, there are dependent plugins, and also conflicting objects or variables. There might be a host of other issues, but overall people should be more satisfied with the experience of getting new plugins. I would really like to have a plugin that concatenates the plugin authors to a page with the license information. Give credit where credit is deserved.
